questions.def: 'Could' + base form' expresses past inability.
questions.question: Despite intensive training, she couldn't ___ the marathon.

questions.def: Inversion after 'only' requires auxiliary 'did'.
questions.question: Only with considerable effort ___ he manage to finish the project.

questions.def: 'Has mastered' implies current relevance of past ability.
questions.question: He ___ the skill after years of practice.

questions.def: 'Unable' expresses a lack of ability.
questions.question: They were ___ to access the restricted files.

questions.def: 'Are capable of' requires a gerund; 'are capable to' requires infinitive.
questions.question: Few employees ___ operate this complex machinery.

questions.def: 'Was able to demonstrate' implies specific past instance.
questions.question: He ___ exceptional talent from a young age.

questions.def: 'Can' expresses general ability or possibility.
questions.question: With proper training, anyone ___ learn a new language.

questions.def: 'Regret + gerund' describes regret about something in the past.
questions.question: I regret ___ to attend the conference due to prior commitments.

questions.def: 'Were able' shows completed ability in a specific past situation.
questions.question: They ___ to secure funding for the project.

questions.def: 'Can' expresses current general ability.
questions.question: Having practiced for years, she ___ play the piano flawlessly.

questions.def: 'Is able to' expresses ability; avoid redundant 'can to'.
questions.question: The software ___ process large amounts of data quickly.

questions.def: 'Can' and 'be able' are redundant. Choose only one.
questions.question: He can be able to speak three languages fluently.

questions.def: Inversion after 'only' + 'was he able to' expresses past ability.
questions.question: Only through perseverance ___ in achieving his goals.

questions.def: 'Am able to' expresses ability; avoid 'can to'.
questions.question: I ___ assist you with that task.

questions.def: 'Wasn't able to' indicates specific past inability.
questions.question: Not having studied, I ___ answer the question.

questions.def: 'Is capable of overcoming' shows general ability.
questions.question: With determination, she ___ any obstacle.

questions.def: 'Cannot' expresses current inability.
questions.question: Due to unforeseen circumstances, we ___ complete the project on time.

questions.def: 'Became able to' expresses a change in ability.
questions.question: He ___ speak Spanish fluently after living in Spain.

questions.def: Inversion after 'only' + 'was he able to' shows ability.
questions.question: Only after years of study ___ the language.

questions.def: 'Could have' expresses past potential ability.
questions.question: She ___ have solved the problem if she had tried harder.

questions.def: 'Is now able to' indicates current ability gained recently.
questions.question: He ___ use the software effectively after the training session.

questions.def: 'Are unable to access' expresses a current lack of ability.
questions.question: Without a password, they ___ the system.

questions.def: 'Managed' shows that she completed her goal.
questions.question: Despite the obstacles, she ___ to achieve her goals.

questions.def: 'Are capable of' requires a gerund or noun.
questions.question: Few students ___ solve this complex equation.

questions.def: 'Able' specifies the realized capacity to do something at a particular moment.
questions.question: Having practiced diligently, she was ___ to perform the complex piece flawlessly.

questions.def: 'Failed to' correctly expresses the inability to achieve something.
questions.question: Despite his efforts, he ___ master the advanced techniques.

questions.def: 'Managed' indicates successful achievement of an action.
questions.question: He ___ to complete the project ahead of schedule.

questions.def: 'Could' shows ability under specific condition.
questions.question: Only through perseverance ___ she acquire the skill.

questions.def: 'Cannot' correctly expresses the lack of ability or permission.
questions.question: Without proper training, one ___ not operate this machinery safely.

questions.def: 'Enough' follows the adjective, so it should be 'skilled enough'.
questions.question: Being enough skilled, she was selected for the role.
